content.value_statement: GTM context can become inconsistent when organization files, members, and Git history are managed manually. This skill guides creation, updates, validation, migration, and repair with clear approvals.
actual_capabilities: Creates a structured Markdown GTM workspace for an organization.
Adds and maintains organization nodes and member records.
Imports existing folders or repositories without changing the source copy.
Validates workspace structure, legacy paths, links, and Git health.
Migrates supported legacy organization and member layouts.
Prepares local Git commits and requests approval before pushing.
limitations: It does not define or validate ICP, persona, or workflow content.
It needs Git for local repository lifecycle operations.
It uses only safe public sources and user-supplied information for research.
Whole-workspace deletion requires a keyboard surface and typed confirmation.

use_cases.title: Start a new organization workspace
use_cases.description: Create a Git-backed GTM workspace with organization facts, member records, and standard contract files.

use_cases.title: Clean up an inherited workspace
use_cases.description: Import an existing folder, identify supported legacy layouts, and propose a safe migration.

use_cases.title: Check workspace health
use_cases.description: Inspect organization structure, member placement, safe links, and Git readiness before continuing GTM work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GTM workspace for Northstar Labs. Our website is https://northstarlabs.example.

prompt_templates.title: Add a member
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Priya Shah, priya@example.com, Head of Sales, to the Northstar Labs GTM workspace.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and repair
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a doctor check on the selected GTM workspace. Describe every issue and propose only safe repairs.

prompt_templates.title: Import and migrate
prompt_templates.prompt: Import this existing GTM folder, inspect it without changing the source, and propose a migration to the current workspace structure.

output_examples.input: Create a GTM workspace for Northstar Labs.
output_examples.output: A concise intake request for the organization name, website, sources, suborganizations, and member details.

output_examples.input: Run a doctor check on the workspace.
output: A plain-language health report with healthy checks and defects.
A single approval proposal for any safe repairs.

best_practices: Provide the organization name and public website in the first request.
Review the proposal card before approving a Git push.
Use doctor before major changes to an inherited workspace.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to create ICP, persona, or workflow content.
Do not provide URLs that contain credentials, tokens, or invitation codes.
Do not request whole-workspace deletion without reviewing the consequence report.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages the organization-level GTM workspace, its member records, standard files, and supported lifecycle operations.

faq.question: Does it create ICPs or personas?
faq.answer: No. It preserves their workspace locations but hands their content lifecycle to dedicated skills.

faq.question: When does it push changes?
faq.answer: It prepares and inspects a local commit first. It pushes only after the user approves the proposal card.

faq.question: Can it import an existing folder?
faq.answer: Yes. It inventories the source, proposes a target and any conversions, and leaves the original folder unchanged.

faq.question: How does it handle unknown facts?
faq.answer: It keeps unresolved required research fields visible as Unknown instead of inventing details.

faq.question: Can it delete a workspace?
faq.answer: Yes, on a keyboard surface after a consequence report and an exact typed organization slug confirmation.
